correctness.rationale: In barycentric subdivision every simplex is a strict chain, and a setwise stabilizer fixes all its vertices (face cardinalities distinguish them). The geometric quotient has one open cell per orbit, with signed chain deletions; no degree associated to a stabilizer multiplies an incidence. The multiset of directed birth-color words classifies exactly these orbits, including isolated vertices as the remaining label budget. I independently generated actual chains of arc-subsets using one maximal-face representative for each path-size partition and canonicalized by its equal-size-path stabilizer. I computed ranks and integral invariant factors of each original differential separately. Torsion in H_d equals torsion of coker(∂_{d+1}), since the quotient by the embedded H_d is im(∂_d), which is free. The sole nonunit factors were 2 in ∂₂ at n=4 and 2 in ∂₄ at n=6 and 7; the ranks recovered all stated free summands, including the mixed H₃ at n=6. H₀ is Z at every size, and there are no cells beyond dimension n−2.
residual_risks: Finite exact calculation only; not a formal proof certificate or a homotopy classification. No inference for n≥8.

value.rationale: Geometric quotients of this canonical relabeling action differ from invariant homology of the ordered complex. The finite first-size classification finds integral phenomena invisible to rational top homology: order-two classes appear, disappear, and reappear across the range, with mixed free/torsion H₃ at n=6. This is a concrete benchmark for studying the nonfree quotient action.
residual_risks: No pattern for larger n or topological classification of attaching maps is established.
